title: The tenant mail transport applies per notification
detail: r.notification(name, { tenantTransport: true }) marks a notification whose mails go through the tenant's own mail transport. channel-email consults its tenantTransport resolver only for these (also under a renamedFrom name); every other notification, such as password reset or sign-in mails, always takes the app transport, even when the tenant has a provider. With tenantTransport set, transport may be omitted: a mail that then has no transport fails with missing_credentials instead of throwing. The template test mail (template-resolver send-test) now gets the tenant config in its channel context and uses the template's notification, so it leaves through the same transport as the real mail.
migration: Apps that pass tenantTransport to createChannelEmailFeature add `tenantTransport: true` to every r.notification whose mails should go through the tenant's provider; without the flag those mails now go through the app transport. Apps without an app SMTP server can drop transport and keep tenantTransport.

title: Email channel can send through the tenant's own mail provider
detail: EmailChannelOptions gets tenantTransport, a resolver called per send with the delivery channel context. mail-foundation exports tenantMailTransport for it: a tenant with a provider configured sends through its own transport, a broken provider fails the send, a tenant without a provider uses the app transport. The transport is built per send and never cached, and the tenant comes from the server-side delivery context only. ChannelContext now carries the tenant's config accessor as config. Without tenantTransport nothing changes.

title: SMTP display names drop address-like characters, inline images get matching extensions
detail: Control characters, angle brackets and at signs in a From display name are replaced by spaces so it cannot smuggle a second address; inline image file names derive their extension from the shared image format list.

title: List-Unsubscribe accepts an app-owned unsubscribe URL
detail: When unsubscribeUrl in the mail data points to an http(s) URL outside the framework unsubscribe route, the email channel sets List-Unsubscribe to that URL without the one-click List-Unsubscribe-Post header, because the framework cannot vouch for a foreign endpoint accepting POST. Other schemes set no header.

title: A mail whose file attachment is missing fails at once instead of retrying
detail: A missing or foreign-tenant file ref ends the delivery attempt as failed (send_failed) without a retry. The send job no longer throws, so the idempotency key is released and the caller can resend. A template test mail whose template file is missing now answers not_sent instead of channel_error.

title: A notification without a mail template fails on the email channel
detail: The renderer option of createChannelEmailFeature is removed. A notification routed to the email channel without template + meta fails its delivery permanently with "has no mail template, declare template + meta on r.notification". r.notification declares no channels, so this is not checked at boot; an app's own mail tests over the inmemory transport catch it.
migration: Drop the renderer option. Declare template + meta (or localizedTemplate) and variables on every r.notification that reaches the email channel, or accept that its email delivery fails. Run the app's notification tests after the bump: every email notification without a template now fails there.

title: Email channel sends rendered-pdf attachments
detail: The channel resolves rendered-pdf entries from notify data next to file entries; without a locale the message locale is used. A render failure fails the send job, so the retry runs it again.

title: Email channel sends file attachments and inline cid images
detail: EmailMessage.attachments is sent through the SMTP transport (inline images with Content-ID). notify data.attachments with kind file entries are resolved through the file store; the PII guard rejects ciphertext file names.

title: Mails get a plain-text part (EmailMessage.text, NotificationRenderer.renderText, simple renderer and GDPR mails fill it)
detail:
Email text part
`EmailMessage` gets an optional `text`. With it the SMTP transport sends `multipart/alternative` with a plain-text part. `NotificationRenderer` gets an optional `renderText`, which the email channel sends next to the HTML through the queued render and send jobs. `createSimpleRenderer` implements it from the template data (header, sections, footer, branding footer; buttons as `label: url`). The GDPR default mails return and send `text` as well. The PII guard checks and redacts `text` like the body.

title: Email channel decrypts the resolved recipient address so notify to users and tenants works with an active KMS
detail:
Email notifications to resolved users reach the plaintext address under an active KMS
With an active PII KMS, an app's `resolveEmail` that reads the stored `user.email` returns ciphertext, and the PII guard rightly refused to send it (`recipient address is a PII ciphertext`). That broke every `notify` target that resolves an address from a user id: a single user, a list of users and `{ tenant }`. The email channel now decrypts the resolved address (`decryptStoredPii`, a no-op without KMS or for plaintext) before it is used for delivery, opt-out checks and the attempt log. The guard is unchanged.
migration: No action needed. Apps whose resolveEmail returns the raw stored user.email now send to the plaintext address instead of failing with "recipient address is a PII ciphertext".

title: EmailMessage.fromName sets the From display name
detail:
channel-email: fromName sets the display name of the From header
`EmailMessage` gets an optional `fromName`, and the email channel passes `data.fromName` through like `replyTo`. The SMTP transport combines it with the address of `message.from` or the transport default, so `from: "App <noreply@x>"` plus `fromName: "Tenant via veridom"` sends from `noreply@x` under the new name. Control characters in the name are replaced by spaces before sending, and an empty name behaves like no name. The PII ciphertext guard refuses a ciphertext `fromName`.

title: Explicit List-Unsubscribe headers replace the automatic pair case-insensitively
detail: The email channel now matches explicit `data.headers` case-insensitively against the automatic unsubscribe headers. Overriding `List-Unsubscribe` or `List-Unsubscribe-Post` in any spelling drops the whole automatic pair, so a mail client no longer sends a one-click POST to a URL that cannot handle it.

title: Automatic List-Unsubscribe / List-Unsubscribe-Post headers for messages that carry a framework unsubscribeUrl
detail:
`createEmailChannel`'s `send()` now sets `List-Unsubscribe: <url>` and
`List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` whenever the
notification's `data.unsubscribeUrl` is an `http(s)` URL whose path is
the delivery feature's `DELIVERY_UNSUBSCRIBE_PATH` — only that route can
honor a one-click POST. An explicit `data.headers["List-Unsubscribe"]`
(or `-Post`) still wins over the automatic value. Apps whose
`unsubscribeUrl` points somewhere else (their own page, a foreign path)
get no automatic headers.
migration:
No action needed for apps already using the framework's unsubscribe
route via `data.unsubscribeUrl`. Apps with a GET-only unsubscribe page of
their own keep getting no `List-Unsubscribe-Post` header, since a
one-click POST there would 404 or no-op.
